1.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother. To the church of God in Corinth, and to all God's people throughout Achaia:
May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.
Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! He is the Father of tender mercy and all comfort.
God comforts us in every single hardship we face. Then we can comfort other people facing hard times. We share with them the exact comfort God gave us!
For just as we share in the many sufferings of Christ, so also through Christ we share in much comfort.
If we suffer, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which helps you patiently bear the same sufferings we suffer.
Our hope for you is firm, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, you also share in our comfort.
Brothers and sisters, know about the terrible troubles we suffered in Asia. The crushing burden was far beyond our ability to endure. We even gave up hope of staying alive!
Inside our hearts, we felt sentenced to death. This happened so we would stop trusting in our own strength. Instead, we learned to trust God, who raises the dead!
He rescued us from such deadly danger, and He will rescue us again. We have set our hope on Him that He will keep on rescuing us,
as you help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks on our behalf for the gift of grace given to us in answer to many prayers.

Now this is what we are proud of, and our conscience agrees: we have lived in the world, and especially toward you, with honesty and godly sincerity. We have not depended on worldly wisdom, but on God's grace.
For we do not write you anything you cannot read and understand. And I hope that you will understand fully,
as you have understood us in part, so that you can be proud of us, just as we will be proud of you on the day of our Lord Jesus.
Because I was sure of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might be blessed twice.
I planned to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and again on my way back, so that you could help me on my journey to Judea.
Did I change my travel plans carelessly? Do I act like worldly people, saying "Yes" and "No" at the same time?
No! As surely as God is faithful, our message never flips back and forth.
Jesus Christ, God's Son, is not wishy-washy. In Christ, God's answer is always a solid "YES!"
Every single promise God made finds its "Yes" in Christ. Through Christ, we say "Amen" to bring glory to God.
Now it is God who makes both us and you stand firm in Christ. He anointed us,
God stamped His official seal of ownership on us. He placed the Holy Spirit inside our hearts. The Spirit is God's down payment, guaranteeing all His future promises!
I call God as my witness — and I stake my life on it — that it was to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
Not that we rule over your faith, but we work together with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.

2.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.
If I make you sad, who will cheer me up? Only you can make me glad, but I made you grieve!
I wrote that difficult letter to avoid a painful visit. When I visit, you should bring me great joy, not sadness! I was confident that all of you would share my happiness.
I wrote to you out of great trouble and pain in my heart, with many tears — not to make you sad, but to let you know how much I love you.
Suppose that one man caused deep sorrow. He did not hurt just me; he hurt all of you!
The punishment the church gave him was severe enough.
Now you must turn around and forgive him! Comfort him so excessive sorrow does not completely crush him.
I beg you to openly reaffirm your love for him!
I wrote to test you and to see whether you would obey in everything.
Whenever you forgive that man, I forgive him too! I forgive him in the presence of Christ for your benefit.
We must do this so Satan does not outsmart us! We know the devil's sneaky plans and evil schemes.
When I went to Troas to preach the good news of Christ, and the Lord opened a door for me there,
I still had no peace of mind, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
Praise God! In Christ, He always leads us in victory! Everywhere we travel, God uses us to spread the sweet knowledge of Him.
We are like a sweet-smelling incense offering of Christ to God.
To those heading for destruction, we smell like rot and death! To those being saved, we smell like fresh, life-giving air! Who is truly qualified for such a high calling?
Unlike so many, we do not sell the word of God for profit. Instead, we speak in Christ before God with sincerity, like people sent from God.

3.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Are we starting to praise ourselves again? Or do we need letters of recommendation to you, or from you, as some people do?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

You clearly show that you are a letter from Christ! We helped deliver this living letter to the world. It was not written using messy pen and ink. The Spirit of the living God wrote it! It was not carved into hard stone tablets. It was engraved directly on human hearts!
We have this confidence before God through Christ.
Not that we are able by ourselves to claim that anything comes from us. Our ability comes from God.
He has made us able to be servants of a new agreement — not of the written law, but of the Spirit. For the written law kills, but the Spirit gives life.

The old Law was carved in letters on stone. That Law brought death, yet it arrived with shining glory! Moses' face beamed so brightly the Israelites could not look at him. Yet that shining glory was already fading away.
How much more glorious is the work of the Holy Spirit!
The old Law condemned people to death. The new covenant makes people completely right with God!
In fact, what was once glorious has no glory now, compared with the far greater glory.
And if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of what lasts!
So, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
We are not like Moses. Moses put a cloth veil over his face. He did this so the people would not watch the glory fade away.
Even today, their stubborn minds remain covered. Only Christ can tear that heavy veil away.
Whenever they read the Old Testament Law, that veil covers their hearts!
Whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil disappears!
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

Our faces are completely uncovered! All of us reflect the dazzling glory of the Lord. The Lord, who is the Spirit, is transforming us. He is changing us to look just like Christ! He fills us with brighter and brighter glory!

4.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: So, since God in His mercy has given us this work, we do not give up.
Instead, we have given up shameful, secret ways. We do not use tricks, and we do not twist the word of God. By clearly telling the truth, we let everyone's conscience judge us in the sight of God.
And even if our good news is hidden, it is hidden to those who are being lost.

Satan, the god of this evil world, has blinded unbelievers! He blocks them from seeing the light of the good news. They cannot see the glorious light of Christ. And Christ shows us exactly what God is like!
For we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.

God commanded long ago: "Let light shine out of darkness!" Now He has made His bright light shine inside our hearts. He lets us see the radiant glory of God. We see that dazzling glory shining in the face of Jesus Christ!
But we have this treasure in clay jars, to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.
Troubles push against us from every side, but we are not crushed! We are confused, but we never give up in despair.
Enemies hunt us down, but God never abandons us. We get knocked down, but we are never destroyed!
We face death daily in our physical bodies, just like Jesus did. We endure this so the life of Jesus will shine in our bodies!
Every day we risk our lives for the sake of Jesus. This shows His supernatural life inside our dying human bodies.
So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
The Scripture says: I believed, and so I spoke. With that same spirit of faith, we also believe, and so we speak,
because we know that the One who raised the Lord Jesus from death will also raise us with Jesus and bring us, together with you, into His presence.
All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is reaching more and more people may cause thanksgiving to overflow, to the glory of God.
That is why we never give up! Our physical bodies are wearing out and growing weaker. Yet inside, God renews our spirit brand new every single day!
Our troubles right now are small and last only a short moment. These small troubles produce for us a glory that outweighs everything! That glorious reward will last forever and ever.
So we do not focus on visible things we can see with our eyes. We focus our eyes on invisible things we cannot see! Earthly things quickly pass away, but heavenly things last forever.

5.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: We know our earthly bodies are like temporary camping tents. One day this earthly tent will be taken down. When that happens, God will give us a permanent home in heaven! Human hands did not build this house; God made it forever.
Right now, we groan inside this fragile body.
We long to put on our brand-new heavenly body like clean clothes.
Then our mortal dying bodies will be completely swallowed up by life!
It is God who has prepared us for this very thing, and He has given us His Spirit as a guarantee of what is to come.
So we are always confident. We know that as long as we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
For we live by faith, not by sight.
So we are confident, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
So we make it our goal to please Him, whether we are at home in the body or away from it.

Every single one of us must stand before the judgment seat of Christ. Christ will evaluate everything we did in our physical bodies. He will reward each person for what they did, whether good or evil.
So, because we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade people. What we are is plain to God, and I hope it is also plain to your consciences.

We are not trying to praise ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you a reason to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in what is in the heart.
If we are out of our minds, it is for God; if we are in our right minds, it is for you.
For the love of Christ controls us, because we are convinced that one died for all, and so all died.
And He died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
So from now on we do not judge anyone by human standards. Even though we once thought of Christ in that way, we do so no longer.
Anyone who belongs to Christ is a brand-new creation! The old, sinful life is gone forever. A fresh, brand-new life has begun!
All of this is God's wonderful gift. Through Christ, God made peace between us and Himself.
God was in Christ, making peace with the whole world! He stopped counting people's sins against them. And He gave us the sacred job of sharing this message of peace!
So we are official ambassadors sent directly by Christ! God is speaking His urgent appeal through us. On behalf of Christ, we beg you: Make peace with God!
Christ never committed a single sin. Yet God placed all our sin on Him for our sake! He did this so in Christ, we could become completely right with God.

6.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: As God's fellow workers, we beg you not to receive God's grace and then waste it.
For God says: At the right time I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you. I tell you, now is the right time; now is the day of salvation.
We do not put anything in anyone's way, so that no one can find fault with our work.
Instead, in every single circumstance, we prove we serve God. We patiently endure extreme troubles, hardships, and disasters.
Mighty mobs beat us, throw us into prison, and riot against us. We work exhausted, go without sleep, and endure hunger.
We prove ourselves through pure living, true knowledge, patience, and kindness. We serve by the Holy Spirit and through sincere, genuine love.
We speak God's truth, powered by His mighty strength! We hold weapons of righteousness in our right hand and left hand!
People honor us, and people insult us. Some tell evil lies about us, while others speak well of us. Critics call us fakes, yet we always tell the truth!
The world ignores us, yet God knows us completely. We face death daily, yet look—we are still alive! Enemies beat our bodies, but God keeps us from death.
Our hearts feel sorrow, yet we overflow with constant joy! We are dirt poor, yet we make many people spiritually rich! We own nothing in this world, yet we possess everything!
We have spoken openly to you, dear Corinthians, and opened our hearts wide to you.
We are not holding back our love for you, but you are holding back your love for us.
I am speaking to you as my children: open your hearts wide to us in return.
Do not team up with unbelievers like mismatched work animals! How can doing right partner with doing evil? How can bright light live together with pitch darkness?
What agreement can exist between Christ and the devil? What does a true believer share with an ungodly unbeliever?

What partnership can the temple of God have with dirty idols? We are the holy temple of the living God! As God has said: I will live with them and walk among them. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
So: Come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch anything unclean, and I will welcome you.
And: I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.

7.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: Dear friends, since we have these promises, let us make ourselves clean from everything that dirties the body and the spirit. Let us aim for complete holiness out of respect for God.
Open your hearts to us. We have wronged no one, ruined no one, and cheated no one.
I am not saying this to blame you. As I said before, you are in our hearts, so that we would live or die together with you.
I speak to you very openly, and I am very proud of you. I am greatly encouraged, and in all our troubles my joy knows no limits.
When we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest. Troubles attacked us from every direction! We faced dangerous battles on the outside. We wrestled with deep fears on the inside!
But God, who comforts those who are discouraged, comforted us by the arrival of Titus.
And not only by his coming, but also by the comfort you had given him. He told us how much you long for me, how sorry you are, and how concerned you are for me. So I was happier than ever.
Even though my letter made you sad, I do not regret it. I did regret it for a while, because I see that the letter hurt you, but only for a little while.
Now I am truly glad! I am not happy that you felt pain. I am glad your sorrow led you to turn back to God. You felt the kind of godly sorrow that God desires!
Godly sorrow leads to true repentance and eternal salvation. That kind of sorrow leaves zero regrets! Worldly sorrow only brings bitterness and death.

Look at what this godly sorrow produced inside you! It made you serious and eager to clear your name. It produced righteous anger against that wicked sin! It filled you with holy fear and deep longing. It gave you passionate concern and a desire for justice. In every way, you proved you are innocent in this matter.
So even though I wrote to you, it was not mainly because of the one who did the wrong, or the one who was hurt. I wrote so that you could see for yourselves, before God, how much you care for us.
All of this brought us tremendous comfort and encouragement! Even better, we saw how overflowing with joy Titus was! All of you refreshed his spirit completely.
I had bragged to Titus about your faith, and you proved me right! Just as our message to you was true, my boasting to Titus was true!
And his love for you is even greater when he remembers how all of you obeyed, welcoming him with respect and care.
I am glad that I can have complete confidence in you.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Smoothed from heavy noun repetition ('the Macedonian churches...the Macedonian churches', 'the Corinthians...the Corinthians') back to natural pronoun flow after each subject is first established, matching the site's standard elsewhere.

verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I want you to know about God's amazing grace. God poured out His grace on the churches in Macedonia!
They suffered great trouble, but they had great joy. They were very poor, yet they gave generously, like rich people give.
I am an eyewitness to their incredible generosity. They gave as much as they were able, and even more than they were able. They gave willingly.
They urged me and my companions strongly, asking us to accept the gift, because they wanted to share in helping God's people.
They did more than we expected. First they gave themselves to the Lord. Then they gave themselves to us, because God willed it.
So we asked Titus to finish what he had started. Titus had already begun this gift of grace among you.
You excel in many things: faith, speech, knowledge, diligence, and love for us. I urge you to excel in giving too.
I am not commanding you. I mention other believers' diligence to test the genuineness of your love.
You know the incredible grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Though He was fabulously rich, He became poor for your sake! Through His poverty, He made you spiritually rich forever.
I give you advice that will help you. Last year you were the first to want to give, and you started giving.
Now you must finish the task. You were eager to begin; now you must finish, giving from what you have.
If a person has an eager heart, God accepts the gift based on what the person has, not on what the person lacks.
I do not want others to be relieved while you suffer hardship. I want complete fairness among God's people!
Right now, you have plenty to supply their desperate need. Later on, their abundance can supply your need.
The Scripture says: "The person who gathered much had nothing left over. And the person who gathered little had plenty to eat!"
I thank God. God put the same diligent care for you into Titus's heart.
Titus accepted my urging. He was diligent, so he went to you on his own initiative.
We sent a brother with Titus. All the churches praise him for his gospel work.
More than that, the churches chose him to travel with us. He helps carry out the gift, for the Lord's glory, and to show your eagerness.
We want to protect our reputation from any dishonest blame. No one can accuse us of stealing a penny from this large gift!
We make sure everything is completely honest before the Lord and people.
We sent another brother with Titus and the first brother. We have tested him many times and found him diligent. Now he is even more diligent, because I have great confidence in you.
If anyone asks about Titus: he is my partner and helper concerning you. If anyone asks about the brothers: they are messengers of the churches and bring honor to Christ.
Therefore, show these men, and show the churches, proof of your love. This proof will confirm my boasting about you.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Smoothed from heavy noun repetition back to natural pronoun flow after each subject is first established, matching the site's standard elsewhere.

verses.text: I really do not need to write to you about this offering for God's people.
I already know your eager enthusiasm! I boast about you to the Macedonians all the time, saying Achaia was ready a year ago. Your enthusiasm has motivated many people.
Still, I sent the brothers so my boasting about you will not prove empty. I want you to be ready, as I said.
If Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we would be ashamed. You would also be ashamed.
So I thought it was necessary to urge the brothers to go ahead to you. I wanted them to arrange your promised gift ahead of time, ready as a generous gift, not squeezed out by greed.
Remember this truth: Whoever plants sparingly harvests sparingly. Whoever plants generously harvests a massive crop!
Each of you must give what you decided in your heart. Do not give reluctantly or under pressure. God passionately loves a cheerful, joyful giver!
God can make all grace overflow toward you. Then you will always have enough of everything, and can overflow in every good work.
Scripture says: “The righteous person scattered gifts everywhere; the righteous person gave to the poor. This righteousness remains forever.”
God supplies seed for the farmer and bread for food. He will supply and multiply your seed for planting. He will increase the harvest of your righteousness!
God will enrich you in every way so you can be generous. This generosity causes thanksgiving to God through us.
This service does two things: it supplies what God's people lack, and it produces many thanksgivings to God.
Through this proof of service, God's people will glorify God — because you obey the gospel of Christ, and because you share generously with God's people and with everyone.
God's people will also pray for you. They will long for you because of the abundant grace of God in you.
Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: I appeal to you with the gentleness and kindness of Christ. Some say I am timid and quiet when facing you in person. They claim I act bold and brave only when writing from far away!
I beg you that, when I come, I will not have to be as bold as I expect to be toward some people who think we live in a worldly way.
For though we live in the world, we do not fight the way the world fights.
The weapons we fight with do not come from this world. Our weapons carry God's power to smash down enemy fortresses!

We smash down rebellious human arguments. We tear down every arrogant barrier raised against the knowledge of God. We capture every rebellious thought like a prisoner of war. We force every thought to submit and obey Christ!
And we are ready to punish every act of disobedience, once your obedience is complete.
You are looking at things only on the surface. If anyone is sure that they belong to Christ, they should remember that we belong to Christ just as much as they do.
So even if I brag a little too much about the authority the Lord gave us — authority to build you up, not to tear you down — I will not be ashamed.
I do not want to seem like I am only trying to scare you with my letters.
Critics sneer: "His written letters are heavy, powerful, and bold. But in person, he looks physically weak and speaks terribly!"
Those critics need to realize an important fact. What we say in our letters from far away, we will back up with bold action when we arrive!
We would never dare rank ourselves with those proud self-promoters! They compare themselves only against their own foolish standards. When they do that, they show they have zero real wisdom!
We, however, will not brag beyond proper limits, but only within the area God has given us, which reaches even to you.
We are not going too far, as we would be if we had not reached you. In fact, we were the first to come to you with the good news of Christ.
We do not brag beyond our limits about work others have done. Our hope is that, as your faith grows, our work among you will greatly expand,
so that we can preach the good news in the regions beyond you. We do not want to brag about work already done in someone else's area.
Whoever wants to boast should boast only about what the Lord has done. Self-praise means nothing!
Only the person whom the Lord praises receives God's true approval.

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness. Yes, please put up with me.
I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. I promised you to one husband, to Christ, so that I could present you to Him as a pure bride.
But I am afraid that, just as the snake fooled Eve by its trickery, your minds may be led away from your sincere and pure love for Christ.

Someone visits you and preaches a fake, different Jesus. You welcome a different spirit than the Holy Spirit you received. You accept a different "good news" than the true Gospel. And you swallow their lies with zero complaint!
But I do not think I am in any way less than those “super-apostles.”
I may not be a trained speaker, but I do have knowledge. We have made this perfectly clear to you in every way.
Was it a sin for me to lower myself in order to lift you up, by preaching the good news of God to you free of charge?
I took pay from other churches, robbing them, so to speak, in order to serve you.

And when I was with you and needed something, I was not a burden to anyone, because the brothers who came from Macedonia gave me what I needed. I have kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and I will keep on doing so.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, no one in the regions of Achaia will stop me from being proud of this.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
And I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to cut the ground out from under those who want a chance to be seen as our equals in the things they brag about.
Those men are phony apostles and deceitful workers. They disguise themselves to look like true apostles of Christ!
This is no surprise to us at all. Even Satan disguises himself as a radiant angel of light!
So his evil servants disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness. In the end, God will punish them for their evil deeds!
I say again: let no one think I am a fool. But if you do, then accept me as a fool, so that I too may do a little bragging.
What I am saying now, I am not saying as the Lord would, but as a fool would, in this confident bragging.
Since many people brag in a worldly way, I will brag too.
You gladly put up with fools, since you are so wise!
In fact, you put up with anyone who makes you a slave, takes advantage of you, traps you, looks down on you, or slaps you in the face.
To my shame, I admit that we were too “weak” for that! But whatever anyone else dares to brag about — I am speaking as a fool — I dare to brag about it too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.

Are they servants of Christ? I sound crazy talking like this, but I have served Him far more! I worked far harder and went to prison more often. Mobs beat me countless times, and I faced death repeatedly.
Five different times, Jewish leaders whipped me with thirty-nine lashes.

Three times Roman soldiers beat me with wooden rods. Once an angry mob stoned me with heavy rocks. Three times I suffered terrifying shipwrecks at sea. I spent a full night and day drifting in deep open water!
I faced flash floods, deadly robbers, and murderous mobs. I faced danger in crowded cities, wild deserts, and stormy seas. I faced danger from treacherous phonies pretending to be believers!
I labored exhausted, froze without warm clothes, and starved without food.
Besides everything else, I face daily pressure: my concern for all the churches.
Who is weak without my feeling weak? Who is led into sin without my burning inside?
If I must brag, I will brag about the things that show my weakness.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In the city of Damascus, King Aretas's governor guarded every gate to arrest me. Believers placed me inside a large rope basket.
They lowered me down through a window in the high city wall! That is how I escaped right out of his greedy hands!

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: I have to keep bragging, even though there is nothing to gain by it. So I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
I know a man in Christ. Fourteen years ago, God snatched him up to the highest heaven! Was he inside his body or outside his body? I do not know. Only God knows!
God carried this man straight into Paradise.
He heard incredible sacred things that human words are not allowed to tell.
I will brag about a man like that, but I will not brag about myself, except about my weaknesses.
Even if I did want to brag, I would not be a fool, because I would be telling the truth. But I hold back, so that no one will think more of me than what they see in me or hear from me.
God gave me wonderful, glorious revelations. To keep me from becoming arrogant, God gave me a sharp thorn in my flesh. It was a tormenting messenger sent from Satan to beat down my pride!
Three different times I begged the Lord to remove this agony.

But the Lord answered me: "My grace is all you need! My divine power works best in your human weakness." So now I brag gladly about my physical weaknesses! That way, the mighty power of Christ can rest over me like a shield.
That is why, for Christ's sake, I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, troubles, and difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
I have made a fool of myself, but you made me do it. You should have been the ones speaking well of me. For I am not in any way less than those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
The marks of a true apostle — signs, wonders, and miracles — were done among you with great patience.
How were you treated worse than the other churches, except that I was never a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!

Now I am ready to visit you for the third time. And I will still refuse to be a financial burden to you! I do not want your money; I want your hearts! Children should not have to save up money for their parents. Parents should save up money to take care of their children!
So I will very gladly spend everything I have, and even spend myself, for you. If I love you more, will you love me less?
Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you. But, you say, I was tricky and trapped you by trickery!
Did I take advantage of you through any of the people I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go to you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not act in the same spirit and follow the same path?
Have you been thinking all this time that we are just defending ourselves to you? We speak before God, as those who belong to Christ. And everything we do, dear friends, is to build you up.

I fear what I might find when I arrive. I might not find you living the way I hope! I dread finding bitter arguing, jealousy, raging anger, and selfish ambition. I fear finding slander, ugly gossip, arrogant pride, and complete disorder!
I fear that my God will humble me before you again. My heart will break over many who fell into gross sin. They have still not repented of their dirty lust, sexual sin, and wild living!

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible.

verses.text: This will be my third visit to you. Every matter must be settled by the word of two or three witnesses.
I already warned those who sinned earlier and all the others, when I was with you the second time. And now, while I am away, I warn them again: when I come back, I will not spare anyone.
You want proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you; He is powerful among you.
For He was crucified in weakness, yet He lives by the power of God. We too are weak in Him, yet by God's power we will live with Him to serve you.
Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless, of course, you fail the test.
And I hope you will see that we have not failed the test.

Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong. We do not pray this so that people will see that we have passed the test, but so that you will do what is right, even if it looks as though we have failed.
For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
We are glad whenever we are weak but you are strong. And our prayer is that you may be fully mature.
This is why I write these things while I am away, so that when I come, I will not have to be harsh in using the authority the Lord gave me — authority to build you up, not to tear you down.
Finally, brothers and sisters, goodbye. Aim for full maturity, listen to my appeal, agree with one another, and live in peace. Then the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
All God's people here send you greetings.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen.
